pipeline.role: Reconstruct repository behavior, capture all evidence of implementation, design, and usage patterns. Document current repo state as-is without interpretation.
outputs: evidence_catalog.json — A comprehensive catalog of all observed behaviors, patterns, and constraints
test_vectors/ — Reference test inputs and expected outputs
public_spec_fragments.json — Extracted domain-level contracts and API signatures
stop_rules: Stop when all code paths have been traced and documented
Stop when evidence is sufficient to hand off to BehaviorModeler without guessing
Stop if more than one interpretation of ambiguous behavior exists; flag as decision point
pipeline.drift_detection: If new code or tests appear that contradict documented behavior, raise a conflict flag immediately
pipeline.handoff_artifact: evidence_catalog.json and public_spec_fragments.json must be semantically complete enough for BehaviorModeler to design a clean-room reimplementation
pipeline.human_checkpoint: Review evidence_catalog.json to ensure all quirks and rough edges are captured, not smoothed away
pipeline.risk_control: Overspecifying is safer than underspecifying. Err on the side of documenting actual observed behavior even if messy

pipeline.persona: API contract designer and behavior specifier
pipeline.role: Read evidence from ReconAndEvidenceCollector and design a clean-room specification that defines the repo's behavior at the contract level, independent of implementation.
outputs: spec.json — A formal behavioral specification covering all public contracts, endpoints, and data flows
interop_tests/ — Test suite that validates any implementation against the spec
stop_rules: Stop when spec.json fully describes all endpoints, data types, and workflows
Stop when interop_tests/ exercises every documented code path
Stop if spec conflicts with evidence; escalate to human
pipeline.drift_detection: Check if spec covers all evidence; if evidence reveals undocumented behavior, amend spec or mark as implementation detail
pipeline.handoff_artifact: spec.json must be language/framework-agnostic and testable by interop_tests/
pipeline.human_checkpoint: Review spec.json to ensure it captures current behavior faithfully without prescribing reimplementation
pipeline.risk_control: Spec should be descriptive (what the repo does) not prescriptive (how to build it differently)

pipeline.role: Use spec.json and interop_tests/ to build a clean-room reimplementation from scratch, without referring to original source code. Validate implementation against spec.
inputs: evidence_catalog.json (reference only, do not copy code)
outputs: ci/ — CI/CD pipeline that runs interop_tests/ and other validations
interop_report.html — Report on whether implementation passes interop_tests/ and matches spec
stop_rules: Stop when implementation passes all interop_tests/
Stop when implementation behavior is semantically equivalent to original (within spec tolerance)
Stop if any gap between spec and implementation is found; escalate
pipeline.drift_detection: Run interop_tests/ after any implementation change; if a test fails, the implementation has drifted from spec
pipeline.handoff_artifact: interop_report.html must show 100% pass rate on interop_tests/ or flag gaps clearly
pipeline.human_checkpoint: Review interop_report.html before accepting implementation. If pass rate is not 100%, request ReimplementationAndTestHarness to fix gaps
pipeline.risk_control: Err on the side of stricter tests. If interop_tests/ are lenient, reimplementation could hide behavior divergence

artifact_inventory.evidence_catalog.json: Comprehensive evidence of current repo behavior and patterns
artifact_inventory.test_vectors/: Canonical test inputs and expected outputs for all major code paths
artifact_inventory.public_spec_fragments.json: Extracted API contracts and data models from original code
artifact_inventory.interop_tests/: Test suite that validates any implementation against spec
